disclosed: TestAllThreadsSyscall (cgo-configuration): The converted corpus is behaviourally a cgo-LINKED Go build for this package, and the oracle is pinned cgo-OFF; this verdict is the residue of that mismatch, not a capability gap. Measured at the pinned state (go1.23.12 linux/amd64, Release, tiering off): Go=pass, C#=skip. Go passes because at CGO_ENABLED=0 its runtime really does stop the world and replay the syscall on every thread. The converted side skips because runtime_doAllThreadsSyscall answers ENOTSUP -- and that is not a stub evading the question: ENOTSUP is the answer a cgo-linked Go build gives, which is why this very test opens by skipping on it with the message pinned as this entry's signature. Go's own source names the configuration in that string. Since the cgocaller keystone's Linux increment 1, the corpus is unambiguously that configuration in BOTH halves -- the nine credential wrappers route through libc's setxid broadcast (TestSetuidEtc passes, 21 assertions) AND the raw AllThreadsSyscall answers ENOTSUP -- so the two facts are coherent rather than the lone gap they were before. The oracle cannot be moved to match: the corpus's Go FILE SELECTION was emitted at CGO_ENABLED=0, both comparison sides must share one cgo state, and the converted side can only be the corpus's. SCOPE NOTE: at cgo-ON the oracle would itself be cgo-linked and skip here too, so the row would read skip/skip and AGREE -- but that agreement would be a coincidence of errno rather than evidence of fidelity, which is precisely why this is disclosed rather than pinned away by a cgo flag. RETIREMENT: if the managed runtime ever gains a real all-threads broadcast, these three verdicts go pass/pass and this entry retires itself.

TestAmbientCapsUserns (platform-skip): The converted deployment spawns children through posix_spawn(3), and its seam NAMES each SysProcAttr field it cannot express and refuses the request rather than silently ignoring it -- the same structural property os/exec's committed TestCredentialNoSetGroups entry discloses under host-limit (coordinator ruling 2026-08-29), reached here from a second package. That entry names Credential alone because Credential is all its suite reaches; this seam declares refusal for eleven fields and syscall's suite reaches Credential. The child never starts, and this test's OWN error handling converts a failed spawn into a skip -- which is why the same ruled property carries host-limit there (Go=pass/C#=fail) and platform-skip here (Go=pass/C#=skip): the class describes the VERDICT SHAPE, not the root. Go reports pass because a real toolchain build spawns via fork+exec and can apply the field; the converted side reports skip by executing the branch Go's own source wrote for an environment that cannot. Self-retiring in this class's required way: the entry stops firing the moment the spawn seam gains Credential -- no corpus change and no manifest edit. runtime-capability's refusal does not apply: nothing here is unimplemented-but-fixable, and the managed fork-window dance that could express these fields was DELIBERATELY retired for file-descriptor-hygiene soundness, which is a ruled correctness decision rather than an omission. SIGNATURE NOTE: pinned to the seam message ALONE. The raw skip output also carries a pointer address and a random temp path ("skipping: 0x7f...: fork/exec /tmp/gotest.../..."), so a signature taken from it verbatim would match exactly once, ever. Captured from the converted host's own -json stream. Coordinator ruling, 2026-09-02

TestExecPtrace (host-limit): The FOURTEENTH member of the posix_spawn seam in this package and the only one wearing the other verdict shape, which is why it carries a different class from the thirteen beside it. Same structural property throughout: the converted deployment spawns children through posix_spawn(3), and its seam NAMES each SysProcAttr field it cannot express and refuses the request rather than silently ignoring it -- the property os/exec's TestCredentialNoSetGroups entry discloses under this same class (coordinator ruling 2026-08-29). The refused field here is Ptrace, a fifth beyond the four the skips reach (Credential, Cloneflags, Unshareflags, Chroot); a census of the seam shows it declares refusal for eleven. WHY host-limit AND NOT platform-skip, stated so the two entries can be reconciled without rediscovering it: the class describes the VERDICT SHAPE, not the root. The thirteen skips are Go=pass/C#=skip because their tests catch the spawn error and skip; this test lets it surface, so the pair is Go=pass/C#=fail -- which matchTerminalStatuses admits under any class EXCEPT platform-skip, exactly as platform-skip admits only the skip pair. One ruled property, two classes, decided by how each consuming test handles a failed spawn. Signature pinned to the STABLE seam message alone: the raw failure text also carries a pointer address and a temp path ("StartProcess with ptrace enabled failed: fork/exec /usr/bin/sh: ..."), so a verbatim signature would match exactly once, ever. Captured from the converted host's own -json stream. Self-retiring in this class's required way -- it stops firing the moment the spawn seam gains Ptrace, with no corpus change and no manifest edit. Coordinator approval, 2026-09-02

TestPrlimitFileLimit (host-limit): The managed runtime's descriptor floor exceeds 43. The test lowers the process's SOFT RLIMIT_NOFILE to 43 (magicRlimitValue + 1, syscall_linux_test.go:720-734) and then opens two pipes; a Go test binary holds a handful of descriptors, the converted host holds far more -- 163 when GolibTests' LinuxDescriptorLimitTests measured it on the WSL arm (2026-09-23, go1.24.13) -- so the first os.Pipe fails EMFILE here and passes in Go. The CLR's own thread start needs 2 free descriptors under that limit (same arm; a native pthread_create needs none), which is why the test host now restores RLIMIT_NOFILE after each top-level test (testing/HostDescriptorLimit.cs): before that, this one verdict took the rest of the syscall row down with it, OutOfMemoryException out of Thread.StartCore at the next test's start and 19 rows never run. Measured, not argued: the row re-read with the restore in place runs 56 of 56.

TestUnshareUidGidMapping (platform-skip): The posix_spawn seam's Unshareflags refusal, the same field and the same refusal TestUnshare and TestUnshareMountNameSpace disclose above (see TestUnshareMountNameSpaceChroot for the seam's structural property). It was never minted because it never diverged where the Linux row was banked: as ROOT, Go skips it itself (exec_linux_test.go:345, 'fails with privileges'), so the 1.23.12 bank read skip/skip; run unprivileged, as the go1.24.13 Linux leg is, Go passes and the seam skips. Surfaced 2026-09-23 when the descriptor-limit restore let the row run past TestPrlimitFileLimit.
